If damage or destruction to the Leased Premises or the building would require more than ninety (90) days to restore, or if the cost to restore the Leased Premises would exceed ten percent (10%) of the replacement cost of the Leased Premises, Tenant may, in its sole discretion, elect to terminate this Lease by written notice to Landlord given within thirty (30) days after the date of such damage or destruction, in which event any unearned rent paid in advance by Tenant shall be refunded and the Security Deposit shall be returned in full.

Either party may terminate this Lease upon thirty (30) days’ written notice if Landlord reasonably estimates that restoration will require more than one hundred eighty (180) days after the later of receipt of insurance proceeds and required permits. Landlord may also terminate if the casualty is uninsured or underinsured, occurs during the last eighteen (18) months of the Term, affects more than fifty percent (50%) of the building’s replacement cost, or if Landlord’s lender requires insurance proceeds to be applied to the debt. Unearned rent and the unapplied Security Deposit shall be returned after Tenant satisfies its surrender obligations.

Change in Security Deposit.

In the event that: (a) the Base Rent, Direct Costs, or other amounts payable under this Lease is increased; and/or (b) Landlord has applied all (or a portion) of the Security Deposit to an obligation owed to Landlord (as described in Section 9.2); then Tenant shall deposit additional funds with Landlord to increase the total Security Deposit to an amount which bears the same relationship to the adjusted Base Rent, Direct Costs, and other amounts payable under this Lease, as the original Security Deposit bore to the same.  Should Landlord be forced to use some or all of the Security Deposit to satisfy any of Tenant’s obligations under this Lease, then after ten (10) days after Landlord’s written notice, Tenant shall restore the Security Deposit to its proper balance.

The Security Deposit shall not increase automatically with increases in Base Rent, Direct Costs or other amounts. After twenty-four (24) consecutive months with no monetary default, the required Security Deposit shall reduce to one month of then-current Base Rent and Direct Costs, and Landlord shall promptly return the excess to Tenant. After a permitted application under Section 9.2, Tenant may replenish the required balance under a reasonable payment plan to be agreed by the parties, and Landlord shall not unreasonably withhold, condition or delay agreement to that plan.

Section 2.  Landlord’s Remedies.  Upon an uncured Event of Default, Landlord may terminate this Lease upon written notice to Tenant and recover actual damages permitted by applicable law, or, without terminating this Lease, re-enter and relet the Leased Premises on Tenant’s behalf and recover from Tenant any deficiency between the rent due under this Lease and the rent actually collected, in each case subject to Landlord’s duty to use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate its damages, including by making reasonable efforts to relet the Leased Premises promptly following any termination or repossession

however Landlord shall need not prioritize reletting the Leased Premises over other vacancies or to lease it on below-market terms. Furthermore, upon a termination of this Lease resulting from Tenant’s default, Landlord shall be entitled to recover the unamortized portion of the rent abatement and any other transaction costs actually incurred by Landlord in connection with this Lease

No Release of Tenant.    In the event of an authorized Transfer, such Transfer shall not release Tenant or change Tenant’s primary liability under the terms of this Lease.  Landlord’s acceptance of any amount due under this Lease from anyone other than Tenant, shall not serve as a waiver of any of Landlord’s rights under this Lease, and shall not serve as an acknowledgement of a Transfer.  If Tenant’s transferee defaults under this Lease, Landlord may proceed directly against either Tenant or the transferee, without pursuing remedies against the other, and without limiting any of the Landlord’s legal or equitable rights.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, upon an assignment of this Lease to a transferee having a tangible net worth not less than Tenant’s tangible net worth as of the Effective Date, and which assumes Tenant’s obligations under this Lease in writing, Tenant shall be released from all liability under this Lease accruing after the effective date of such assignment.
